clue.text: Character about to hit road

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for about
RD is the standard abbreviation for road

explanation.surface: Someone is on the point of setting off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to hit road' reads as a phrase about leaving; split it, and 'about' meets 'road' head on.
explanation.definitionFit: A card is an informal word for an eccentric or amusing person, a real character.

clue.text: Knot cut when hands change spar

indicators.note: the hands are left and right, so one letter standing for the left hand is swapped for the one standing for the right

parts.note: a bow is a knot with loops, as in a shoelace
to cut or split something apart

explanation.surface: A rope is severed while sailors swap places at a mast.
explanation.walkthrough: In wordplay the hands are left and right, abbreviated L and R; the swap leaves a sprit, itself a small spar.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowsprit is the pole projecting forward from a ship's bow, one of the vessel's spars.

clue.text: Reportedly dispose of monk here?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken or heard, so the word is judged by its sound not its spelling

parts.note: to dispose of goods is to sell them

explanation.surface: A question about where one might get rid of a monk.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a monk lives in a small room of this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is the small private room in a monastery where a monk sleeps and prays.

clue.text: Jumper's odds double

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds in horse racing
a ringer, or dead ringer, is someone's exact double

explanation.surface: A betting tip: the price on a showjumper has doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' suggests a sweater or a horse; here it is anything that springs.
explanation.definitionFit: A springer is something that leaps, such as the springer spaniel or a springbok.

clue.text: Vehicle passes Tesla occasionally

parts.note: to pass away is to die

indicators.note: occasionally means now and then, so only every other letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of the car maker's name

explanation.surface: An ordinary car overtakes an electric Tesla now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tesla makes 'Vehicle' look like part of a motoring scene, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a vehicle such as a car, lorry or train powered by a diesel engine.

clue.text: Put off dance then argue for reparation

parts.note: a disco is a dance party

indicators.note: reparation means mending, so the word is repaired by being rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A night out is postponed and then followed by a row about compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourage is to deter someone, putting them off doing something.

clue.text: LED's dead, eh? Change it

indicators.note: an instruction to alter the preceding words, rearranging their letters

parts.note: the letters of both words, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: A light-emitting diode has failed, so someone suggests replacing it.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make LED look like a light bulb; it is the past tense of lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Headed is a synonym of led, as in heading or leading a team or a procession.

clue.text: Day goes on forever for one in a rut?

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
e'er, the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a dull routine finds every day endless.
explanation.walkthrough: A rut is also the annual mating season of stags, so 'in a rut' is not about boredom.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer are the animals that rut, the males fighting during the autumn breeding season.

clue.text: A&E collecting personal data for software company

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so one part takes the other inside it

parts.note: the letters of the hospital department, without the ampersand
date of birth, a standard item of personal data on forms

explanation.surface: A hospital emergency department gathers patients' details on behalf of a tech firm.
explanation.walkthrough: A&E is accident and emergency, the British hospital casualty department.
explanation.definitionFit: Adobe is the American firm that makes Photoshop and the PDF reader, a well-known software maker.

clue.text: Right Holy Joe inspiring base with energy

indicators.note: inspiring literally means breathing in, so one part draws the other inside it

parts.note: a holy Joe is a sanctimonious person, a prig
base in the sense of low and despicable
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A righteous preacher stirs up a lowly congregation with his energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A privilege is a special right or entitlement granted to a person or group.

clue.text: Refuses to acknowledge record Liam's re-issued

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: something re-issued comes out again in a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the name with its s, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A singer called Liam disowns an album that has been put out again.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Liam Gallagher of Oasis distancing himself from a reissue.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim something is to deny responsibility for or connection with it, refusing to own it.

clue.text: After month in retreat, a glimpse of Ronnie Wood

indicators.note: something in retreat goes backwards, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
taken as written

indicators.note: a glimpse is only a brief first sight, so just the opening letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: After a month in rehab, Rolling Stone Ronnie Wood makes a brief appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ronnie Wood' reads as the guitarist; 'Wood' is detached as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant timber from coniferous trees, used for chests and pencils.

clue.text: German master in German school — it's where you'd expect to see one

definitions.text: school — it's where you'd expect to see one
definitions.note: the answer is the fish found in a school, not the school itself

parts.note: Herr is German for Mr or master
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A German teacher at a German school is just where you would expect him.
explanation.walkthrough: A school is a shoal of fish, so 'school' points to the sea, not a classroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Herring are fish that swim in huge shoals, also called schools.

clue.text: Flemish earthenware drinks bottle

indicators.note: to drink is to take in, so the words around swallow the letters needed

parts.note: running across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A description of a Flemish pottery flask for holding liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, as in losing one's bottle.
explanation.definitionFit: Heart means courage or spirit, the same sense as the informal British bottle.

clue.text: An Asian: one's described by that

indicators.note: to describe a shape is to draw round it, so one part encircles the other

parts.note: 'that' refers back to An Asian, read here as a person from India
the letters of the word with its s, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A remark that one person's Asian identity is captured by that description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' has no meaning of its own: it points back to the definition, standing for a different Asian.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indonesian is a person from Indonesia, a country in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Mysterious appearance of old saint lured pilgrims here?

indicators.note: something mysterious appears in a strange form, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
S is the abbreviation for saint
taken as written

explanation.surface: A miraculous vision of an ancient saint drew pilgrims to a shrine.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, Lourdes became a shrine after visions of the Virgin Mary to Saint Bernadette.
explanation.definitionFit: Lourdes in south-west France is one of the world's great Catholic pilgrimage sites.

clue.text: Bad shot of actor Tom maybe ending up on top

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the start, so the final letter climbs to the front

parts.note: Tom Hanks, the Hollywood actor; maybe flags him as one example of an actor Tom

explanation.surface: A poor photograph of Tom Hanks or a similar actor lands at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a shank is a miss-hit that flies off the heel of the club, a notoriously bad stroke.

clue.text: Played march to end but missed odd bits

indicators.note: dropping the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones from the words before

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters of the run of words

explanation.surface: A band played a march right through but fluffed some passages.
explanation.definitionFit: Acted means performed a role, as an actor plays a part on stage.

clue.text: Not enjoying A Study in Scarlet?

indicators.note: not enjoying something means being without it, so that letter is lost

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
taken as written, the letter to remove

explanation.surface: Someone is not liking the Sherlock Holmes story A Study in Scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: The title A Study in Scarlet must be broken up: 'A' and 'Study' make the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a bright shade of red, so the colour names stand in for each other.

clue.text: The dim and distant past?

parts.note: surface reading: a long-ago time that is hard to remember
setter's reading: dim as unlit, an era named for its supposed lack of learning or light

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dim and distant' is a stock phrase for the long-forgotten past; here 'dim' is taken literally, as gloomy and unenlightened.
explanation.definitionFit: The early medieval period in Europe was traditionally called benighted, seen as lacking culture and records.

clue.text: Set adrift between America and Australia?

indicators.note: placing something between two things puts it inside them
something adrift floats out of place, so these letters drift into another order

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for America
taken as written, then rearranged
A is the abbreviation for Australia

explanation.surface: Someone has been cast off in a boat somewhere between two continents.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reuses the abbreviations: a ship between America and Australia is crossing the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: At sea means out on the ocean, as a voyage across the Pacific would be.

clue.text: Small bolt one's installed for a collector

indicators.note: installed means put in place of something, so one letter takes over another's spot

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a quarrel is a bolt fired from a crossbow
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A little fastener is fitted for someone who collects hardware.
explanation.walkthrough: The I replaces the A of QUARREL; the A is itself 'one', so one one replaces another.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel stores nuts for winter, and figuratively a squirrel is a person who hoards things.

clue.text: Extract of malt is an essential for some infusions

indicators.note: an extract is a part drawn out, so the letters are drawn from inside the following words

parts.note: running from the end of the first word into the last

explanation.surface: Malt extract is a key ingredient in certain brewed drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extract' looks like part of 'malt extract'; it signals letters taken from the words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisanes are herbal teas, drinks made by steeping leaves or flowers in hot water.

clue.text: Forecaster's keeping dry in the sun?

indicators.note: keeping means holding on to, so one part holds the other within it

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
TT means teetotal, someone who stays dry of alcohol

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster predicts it will stay dry in sunshine.
explanation.walkthrough: The sun is defined by example as a setter, since it sets every evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The sun goes down each evening, so it can be called something that sets.

clue.text: Begins as hooker in depleted scrums

indicators.note: one part goes inside the other
depleted means emptied out, so the inside letters go and only the ends are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word
tart is slang for a prostitute, also called a hooker

explanation.surface: A rugby match kicks off with a hooker in weakened scrums.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the hooker is the player in the middle of the front row of a scrum, so the surface is pure rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: Starts and begins are synonyms, both meaning commences.

clue.text: Does partner with this many eggs jump about wildly?

parts.note: roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish
a horse bucks when it leaps and kicks

explanation.surface: A question whether someone's mate will leap around after getting so many eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is the plural of doe, female deer.
explanation.definitionFit: A roebuck is the male roe deer, the mate of the females called does.

clue.text: Scribes gathered they might be the last

indicators.note: gathered here means understood from hearing, so the word is taken by sound

parts.note: a scribe writes, so scribes is a verb meaning writes

explanation.surface: Copyists who were assembled may have been the final ones.
explanation.walkthrough: The last rites are the sacrament given to a dying person.
explanation.definitionFit: Rites are ceremonies, and the last rites are those administered to someone about to die.

clue.text: Vessel's crew initially removed from another …

indicators.note: removed from means taken away out of, so a letter is dropped from the word
initially points to the start of a word, so only its opening letter is the one taken away

parts.note: another vessel, a craft
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A ship's sailors are first taken off and put on a different boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another vessel, so it stands for a second word for a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A raft is a flat floating structure of logs or planks, a simple vessel.

clue.text: Song about gold wagon puzzling South American native?

indicators.note: about means around, so one part surrounds the others

parts.note: an aria is a song in an opera
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a car or wagon, as on a railway

explanation.surface: A song about a golden wagon baffles a native of South America.
explanation.walkthrough: Araucaria is the monkey puzzle tree, native to Chile; it was also the pseudonym of a famous Guardian crossword setter.
explanation.definitionFit: The monkey puzzle tree, genus Araucaria, comes from Chile and Argentina, hence a puzzling South American native.

clue.text: … to then cover boat's prow in varnish?

indicators.note: covering a letter hides it under another, so the letter carried from the previous clue replaces it

parts.note: the word whose first letter, its prow, is covered over

explanation.surface: A continuation: the crew then paint over the front of the boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link it to 26 down: the C (crew initially) taken from CRAFT then covers the B at the prow of BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A coat is a single layer of paint or varnish applied to a surface.

clue.text: Soldiers are regularly taking DNA test

parts.note: A is the symbol for the are, a metric unit of area

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters

explanation.surface: Troops are routinely made to give samples for genetic testing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are' is not a verb here but the metric unit of 100 square metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldier ants are a caste of ant that defend the colony, so ants can be soldiers.

clue.text: Judge cycling to obscure Australian location

indicators.note: cycling means going round, so the last letter moves round to the front

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a game
to mantle is to cover or obscure

explanation.surface: A judge rides a bike to some remote place in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Fremantle is a port city near Perth in Western Australia.

clue.text: Attentive porter possibly has right time

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale, hence possibly
R is the abbreviation for right
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A watchful hotel porter has the correct time.
explanation.definitionFit: Alert and attentive both describe someone watchful and paying close attention.
